title: Desk ships ~601KB of the forbidden editor/crypto graph and the route-bundle gate reports green
description:
The desk route downloads **1.20 MB across 29 requests** to render a list of file names. Roughly **601 KB of that is the exact ProseMirror + markdown-it + @noble crypto + `src/lib/review` graph that `web/scripts/check-route-bundles.mjs` exists to forbid.**

**And the gate reports green.** It walks only *static* imports; the entry `await`s the dynamic one before mount, so the browser fetches it anyway. The CI output says "route bundle boundaries hold" while the network panel says otherwise. A gate that passes while the thing it guards is violated is worse than no gate — it converts an unnoticed regression into a documented guarantee.

Measured consequence: **LCP 8,248 ms** on Fast 3G + 4x CPU throttle, for a page whose entire content is a heading, three cards, and a list of names.

Runtime work is genuinely clean and is not the problem: CLS 0, TBT 3 ms, zero `will-change`, zero `backdrop-filter` on the desk, no layout-property animation, fonts correctly subset with `font-display: swap`. This score is entirely about payload.

Two things to fix, and the second matters more than the first:

1. **Stop pulling the editor graph into the desk route.** The desk needs none of ProseMirror, markdown-it, the crypto suite, or the review layer to list workspaces. Defer them to the point the user actually opens a document.

2. **Fix the gate so it cannot lie again.** Teach `check-route-bundles.mjs` to follow dynamic imports that are awaited before mount, or — more robustly — assert against the *observed network graph* for each route rather than the module graph. The gate is wired into `web/scripts/deploy-browser-staging.mjs:48` before deploy and into `npm run check:route-bundles`, so it is load-bearing infrastructure; it needs to be right.

Worth noting for contrast: the same gate applied to the landing route **is** accurate — that route was independently verified at 25.9 KB brotli of JS with zero requests for ProseMirror / Mermaid / KaTeX / Shiki / @noble / WASM across four device profiles. So the gate works for statically-imported graphs; it is the awaited-dynamic-import path that escapes it.

Suggested command: /impeccable optimize

---
EXACT ROOT CAUSE AND NUMBERS (desk audit, measured cold load, empty desk, 1280x900):

  Total transfer   1,203,516 B across 29 requests (18 script, 6 stylesheet, 3 font, 1 document, 1 icon)
  Static graph per .vite/manifest.json — what the gate measures — 388.8 KB.
  So ~815 KB arrives on the wire that the gate never looks at.

The mechanism is `web/hosted/app/main.ts:41-42`, which AWAITS the dynamic import before mount:

    const { RealWorkspaceAppService } = await import('../../src/hosted/app/real-service');
    service = await RealWorkspaceAppService.open();

Nothing is deferred. The cost was moved off the manifest, not off the wire — and main.ts:5-7 documents the loophole as the design.

`real-service.ts` then statically imports (verified against the build manifest):
  schema-*.js          127 KB  markdown-it (52 modules), prosemirror-markdown/-collab, suggest-changes
  index-*.js            94 KB  prosemirror-view
  index-*.js            86 KB  prosemirror-model/-state/-transform
  browser-share-*.js    69 KB  @noble/hashes, @noble/curves, @noble/ciphers
  browser-session-*.js 202 KB  21 x src/lib/review/*
  real-service-*.js    125 KB  11 x src/lib/review/*
  browser-ws-*.js       23 KB  signaling, ws, device-proof

Five of the six FORBIDDEN_MODULES patterns (check-route-bundles.mjs:23-30) on the wire on every desk load.

WHY THE GATE MISSES IT: `collectStaticFiles()` (check-route-bundles.mjs:94-109) queues only `chunk.imports`. Vite records these under `chunk.dynamicImports`, which is never traversed.

THE PROSEMIRROR HALF IS ONE LINE:
  web/src/lib/review/browser-owner-workspace-runtime.ts:11
  import { markdownSerializer } from '../schema';
Reached statically from real-service.ts. Pulling the markdown serializer into the module that lists workspace names drags 307 KB of ProseMirror + markdown-it onto a page that renders three <strong> tags.

VITALS CONFIRM IT IS PURELY BYTES, NOT WORK:
  FCP 2,388 ms · LCP 8,248 ms · CLS 0 · TBT 3 ms · 1 long task (53 ms), all on Fast 3G + 4x CPU.
  TBT of 3 ms proves this is not a JS execution problem. 1.20 MB over 1.6 Mbps is ~6.0 s of transfer alone.
  Cutting the ~601 KB takes payload to ~600 KB and LCP to roughly 3-4 s; also dropping the bits-ui
  preload below takes it under 450 KB. No rendering or animation optimisation is warranted.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT LEAK — 150 KB of bits-ui for a dialog the desk never renders:
  assets/scroll-viewport-*.js is 149.7 KB / 131 modules (68 x bits-ui, 17 x svelte-toolbelt, 10 x runed,
  @lucide/svelte, tailwind-variants, tabbable, tailwind-merge, plus BottomSheet and the whole
  src/lib/components/ui/dialog/* set). That is 46% of the desk's 326 KB static JS and it is
  modulepreload-ed by dist-browser/app/index.html, so it is fetched at highest priority.
  It arrives because AppShell.svelte:4 statically imports EditorShell.svelte (3,149 lines).
  The gate misses this too — FORBIDDEN_MODULES enumerates vendor packages, not the app's own
  route-level components.
  FIX: make EditorShell a dynamic import in AppShell (it only renders under `editorMode && detail`,
  AppShell.svelte:289). One change drops bits-ui, the dialog set and BottomSheet from the desk preload.

THIRD: the desk ships the entire app stylesheet. assets/app-*.css is 41.4 KB of the route's 62.8 KB.
Roughly 226 of app-shell.css's 2,795 lines are desk rules; the rest is editor, share sheet, thumb dock,
lightbox, review rail, arrival toasts.

The gate DOES correctly keep mermaid, KaTeX and shiki out of the app route — it is the
awaited-dynamic-import path and the app's own components that escape it.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
PARTIAL — 203 KB removed and verified; the rest needs an architectural cut, not an import tweak.

DONE (typechecked, 97/97 unit tests pass):
1. AppShell.svelte no longer statically imports EditorShell. It is loaded on demand via
   `import('./EditorShell.svelte')`, kicked off by an $effect on editorMode so the chunk is in
   flight while the workspace body is still being read. Added an 'editor-loading' branch so the
   unloaded case cannot fall through to 'That workspace isn't here'.
2. browser-owner-workspace-runtime.ts no longer statically imports markdownSerializer; it is
   imported at its single call site inside the already-async commitRolloverAndPublish.

MEASURED, same method as the audit (cold load, 1280x900, networkidle):
  BEFORE  /app  1,203.5 KB  29 requests
  AFTER   /app  1,000.8 KB  32 requests   (script 836.5 KB, css 60.8 KB)
The 149.7 KB bits-ui/dialog/BottomSheet chunk is gone from the desk entirely.
Landing is unaffected: 257.6 KB, 68.8 KB script.

STILL SHIPPING and why I stopped rather than half-doing it:
  schema-*.js 127.1 KB · index-*.js 94.4 KB (prosemirror-view) · index-*.js 86.4 KB (prosemirror-model)
  browser-session-*.js 202.1 KB · real-service-*.js 124.8 KB · browser-share-*.js 69.5 KB

Two further static edges to lib/schema remain:
  browser-local-collab.ts:19    markdownParser (line 308, async loadSeed — deferrable)
                               markdownSerializer (line 363, commitNow — **synchronous**)
  browser-owner-authority.ts:10 markdownParser (line 715, async — deferrable)

commitNow(fileId): void is on the autosave/debounce path and its ordering guarantees around
inflightCommits are load-bearing. Making it async to accommodate a dynamic import changes
collab commit ordering — that is a correctness risk I am not taking blind.

The real fix is higher up and is a genuine refactor: workspace-service.ts:49-52 statically imports
BrowserOwnerWorkspaceRuntime, so the desk drags the whole editor runtime for three read-only calls
(listWorkspaces, storageHealth, getWorkspace). Splitting the read-only service from the editor
runtime cuts all six remaining chunks at once. That wants its own pass with the collab tests green.

GATE NOT YET FIXED. Deliberately not traversing dynamicImports in check-route-bundles.mjs — that
would now flag the two legitimately-lazy chunks created above. The correct gate is a runtime
script-byte budget per route, which measures what actually loads and cannot be gamed by renaming
chunks. Filed as the remaining work here.

title: INK theme has no destructive colour: Delete renders in the primary accent; three tokens undefined
description:
In the INK theme the desk has **no red anywhere in its destructive vocabulary**. Every destructive surface resolves to `--primary-hover`, which in dark mode is the steel-blue accent — so "Delete workspace" and the delete-confirm dialog render in exactly the same hue as the primary "Join" button and every focus ring.

Destructive intent is carried by colour on this surface, and in dark mode that colour is the *affirmative* one. The delete action is irreversible.

Also found on the desk, same pass:

**Three undefined tokens silently resolve to nothing.** `--radius-md`, `--radius-lg` and `--wash` are not defined on this route, so they collapse to `0px` / `transparent`. Nothing errors; corners and washes just quietly do not appear. These are the hardest kind of drift to notice because the page still renders.

**Hairlines are drawn at full-opacity ink.** `.desk-title` and `.storage-panel` use solid `--ink` rather than `--border`, and DESIGN.md specifies hairlines as "ink at low alpha, never a solid gray line". In INK this inverts into the brightest element on the page.

Token discipline in source is otherwise real and worth protecting: exactly **one** literal colour in 2,795 lines of `app-shell.css`, and it is outside the desk. These are drift and undefined-token failures, not hex-code failures.

Fix: introduce a destructive token that survives the theme flip (a red tuned for INK, the way `--green`/`--danger-ink` were tuned for AA), define or remove the three phantom tokens, and move the two hairlines to `--border`.

Suggested command: /impeccable colorize

---
EXACT MEASUREMENTS (desk audit) — resolved through a live probe element in both themes.

DESTRUCTIVE SURFACES, all six using var(--rust-deep), which chrome.css:21 aliases to var(--primary-hover):

  .button.danger            chrome.css:140-142        PAPER oklch(0.42 0.15 28) -> INK oklch(0.78 0.10 220)
  .row-action.danger:hover  app-shell.css:2519-2521   same
  .join-error               app-shell.css:2785-2789   same
  inline import-error       DeskHome.svelte:199       same
                            OpenPage.svelte:75        same
                            StoragePage.svelte:157    same

`--danger-ink` exists for exactly this and IS used correctly at app-shell.css:931-934 for the editor's
entry actions — so the desk is the inconsistent half of the same file.
TOKEN TO USE: var(--danger-ink) for all six (the text-safe tier; chrome.css:23-26 documents that the
accent tier measures 3.0-3.3:1 on 11px badges).

UNDEFINED TOKENS — verified live on the running page:
  --radius-md -> UNDEFINED, border-radius resolves to 0px
  --radius-lg -> UNDEFINED
  --wash      -> UNDEFINED, background resolves to rgba(0,0,0,0)

--radius-md/--radius-lg are declared at web/src/app.css:16-17, which web/hosted/app/main.ts:8-13 never
imports. Loaded sheets on /app, confirmed at runtime: scroll-viewport, theme, app, index, chrome,
bottom-sheet — src/app.css is not among them. Consumers rendering SQUARE where the design intends 8/10px:
  app-shell.css:397 .file-row · :452 .file-add-row · :775 .viewing-safely · :808 .arrival-toast
--wash is consumed at app-shell.css:1482 (.share-selection-actions button:hover) and defined nowhere, so
that hover has no background at all. Intended value is almost certainly var(--accent) (tokens.css:68).
FIX: import ../../src/app.css in the hosted entry, or re-declare the radii in chrome.css alongside the
other hosted aliases.

ONE CLASS, TWO COLOURS — a specificity collision:
  app-shell.css:42-48   .local-badge        { color: var(--green) }        specificity 0,1,0
  app-shell.css:181-184 .workspace-row span { color: var(--hosted-muted) } specificity 0,1,1
The same .local-badge class renders green in the header (AppHeader.svelte:33) and muted grey in the row
(DeskHome.svelte:233); the dot follows it because app-shell.css:54-59 sets background: currentColor.
Net effect: "Shared · relay sees only ciphertext" is visually identical to "Local only", so the one place
ledger green WOULD be legitimate under the Quarantine Rule — the collaboration layer — is the one place it
silently loses. This is the inverse of the header badge issue filed separately, and a separate fix:
raise .local-badge specificity or scope the row rule to `.workspace-row > span`.

HAIRLINES AT FULL-OPACITY INK:
  app-shell.css:102  .desk-title    { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ink) }
  app-shell.css:2224 .storage-panel { border-top: 1px solid var(--ink) }
Measured in INK: oklch(0.87 0.008 250) — a near-white 1px rule, the highest-contrast element on the dark
page, brighter than the h1 it underlines. TOKEN TO USE: var(--rule) (chrome.css:18 = --border = ink 18%).

--rust-deep IS A HOVER TOKEN USED AS A RESTING COLOUR IN 16 PLACES:
  chrome.css:99,141 · app-shell.css:51,306,558,582,1529,1625,2268,2520,2781,2782,2788 ·
  DeskHome.svelte:199 · OpenPage.svelte:75 · StoragePage.svelte:157
chrome.css:21 defines it as var(--primary-hover). That is how one alias came to carry four unrelated
meanings: primary-hover, eyebrow decoration, warning, and danger. Untangling it is the root fix.

LITERAL COLOURS IN app-shell.css — only two are defects, in 2,795 lines:
  :2615 background: rgba(0,0,0,0.86)          .lightbox scrim -> should be var(--overlay-veil)
  :1008 box-shadow: ... oklch(0.2 0.02 55/8%) .editor-top     -> should be var(--shadow-soft) (flips in INK)
  :768  --view-only: oklch(0.55 0.06 230)     documented intentional local token — NOT a defect

CONTRAST: zero failures across twelve state/theme combinations (empty, populated, join panel, join error,
blocked, quota, private, best-effort, demo — light and dark). Lowest on the desk 6.54:1. axe-core confirms
0 violations. The only sub-4.5:1 number anywhere is the disabled .quick caption in the blocked state at
3.13:1 once opacity 0.55 is applied — WCAG 1.4.3 explicitly exempts inactive components, so it is a
legibility note, not a violation.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified by live token probe in both themes. DESTRUCTIVE COLOUR — the six surfaces now use --danger-ink instead of --rust-deep (which aliases --primary-hover, so in INK they rendered the same steel blue as the primary Join button): chrome.css .button.danger app-shell.css .row-action.danger:hover app-shell.css .join-error DeskHome.svelte / OpenPage.svelte / StoragePage.svelte — the three inline error

styles MEASURED (live probe on /app): light --danger-ink oklch(0.45 0.18 27) red (--rust-deep was oklch(0.42 0.15 28)) dark --danger-ink oklch(0.70 0.16 25) red (--rust-deep is oklch(0.78 0.10 220) steel blue) INK now has a real destructive colour. The three inline copies became a .form-error class — the audit's read was right, it was a class copied instead of created. That also removes 3 of the 20 inline style= attributes tracked in .44. UNDEFINED TOKENS — declared in chrome.css beside the other hosted aliases. They were in src/app.css inside a Tailwind block the hosted entries never import, so they resolved to 0px/transparent with no error and no visual alarm: --radius-md now calc(.625rem - 2px) (was UNDEFINED -> 0px; .file-row, .file-add-row rendered square) --radius-lg now .625rem (was UNDEFINED -> 0px; .viewing-safely, .arrival-toast) --wash now var(--accent) (was UNDEFINED -> transparent; .share-selection-actions hover had no background at all) Verified resolving and flipping correctly: --wash is ink 7% in PAPER, white 3% in INK. Derived --radius-* from the same --radius as app.css so the two declarations cannot drift. HAIRLINES — .desk-title border-bottom and .storage-panel border-top moved from solid var(--ink) to var(--rule). DESIGN.md: hairlines are 'ink at low alpha, never a solid gray line'. Measured in INK: now oklch(0.87 0.008 250 / 0.16), previously full opacity — the brightest element on the dark page, brighter than the h1 it underlined. SPECIFICITY COLLISION — added .workspace-row .local-badge { color: var(--green) }. '.workspace-row span' (0,1,1) had been outranking '.local-badge' (0,1,0), so the same class rendered green in the header and muted grey in a row, making 'Shared · relay sees only ciphertext' visually identical to 'Local only' (the dot followed, since it paints with currentColor). svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass. Still open elsewhere in the epic: --rust-deep remains a hover token used as a resting colour in ~13 other places, which is the root cause behind this whole family (tracked in .36).

title: Stop durable relay writes for ephemeral cursor and viewport presence
description: Durable Objects rows_written quota is exhausted because replaceable cursor/view presence falls back to HTTP relay and still writes rate, PoW, sequence, and latest-presence state. Make cursor/view presence WebRTC-only; preserve durable relay delivery for comments and document/review events; reject or safely drop legacy relayed presence before any Durable Object writes.
close_reason: Cursor/view presence is WebRTC-only in browser and native clients; relay rejects V3 presence uploads before Durable Object mutations; durable review events remain relayed; full web and relay suites pass.

title: Stop sharing wedged forever on partially-created shares
description: James: 'why can't I stop sharing.' His share record was stuck mid-publish from the quota era; Stop → deleteRemote tears down remote resources that don't exist → the relay's 404s are CORS-untagged (anti-enumeration) → the browser throws before reading the status → stopShare aborted and kept the record, forever. Fix: the revoke INTENT (revoke_pending tombstone) persists durably BEFORE any network call; remote teardown is now best-effort. Stop always completes locally — if teardown couldn't be confirmed, the tombstone is retained and retried by the next ensureShare (orphaned remote resources die with their TTL at worst). This IS the reset mechanism: Stop always works, then re-share starts clean. New contract test: unreachable teardown → stop completes, tombstone survives, next share retries the delete and recreates.
close_reason: Closed

title: Owner permanently deaf after room instance rotation (seq-binding conflict loop)
description: ROOT CAUSE of James's owner-not-seeing-comments: when the relay room is rebuilt under the same roomId (relay eviction/expiry, or republish recreating a vanished room), the new instance restarts serverSeqs. The owner's IndexedDB still binds those seqs to the dead instance's envelopes, so every inbound envelope fails commitInbound BEFORE dispatch, the ws client closes and reconnects, and the same frame conflicts again — an infinite deaf loop with threads:0 and (pre-diagnostics) zero symptoms. Confirmed by James's __attnInboundErrors ring: 6× 'server sequence is already bound to another envelope' in 20ms. Fix: (1) commit-conflict heal — purge the room's inbound log + cursors (new storage.resetRoomInboundHistory), reset the cursor, re-commit, continue the in-flight replay; (2) hello regression detector — a hello whose serverSeq is below our cursor proves rotation even when no conflict would fire (cursor beyond new head), resubscribes from 0 after the purge. Verified end-to-end locally: relay DO state wiped under a live share, owner reloads, heals, and receives a post-rotation reviewer comment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Joiner page unusable at mobile widths (fixed rail squeezes doc to ~60px)
description: At 390x844 the /s/<id> review page keeps a fixed-width comments rail; the document column collapses to ~60px, one word per line, and the top status strip text overlaps itself. Review links are exactly what people open on phones. Needs responsive stacking (rail as bottom sheet / toggle, like the owner app's mobile shell which is already good).
close_reason: Closed

title: Owner editor rolls back recent edits on layout remount (mobile<->desktop resize)
description: Repro (james/room-as-project-ux, local dev:browser:shares): owner shares a doc, types ' LIVE-EDIT-MARKER-42.' which syncs live to the joiner; resize owner viewport 1440x900 -> 390x844 (mobile shell remount). Owner editor re-renders WITHOUT the marker; joiner keeps it. Resizing back to desktop does not restore it and it never re-converges — owner local state and room state silently diverge, with the owner's own accepted+synced edit lost from their canvas. Data-loss class bug; phone rotation / window resize triggers it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Prevent pending editor changes from being lost on navigation and workspace actions
description: Live staging validation on 2026-07-11 reproduced durable data loss with real keyboard input. Type into ProseMirror and immediately reload or select another file: the header still says Saved on this device, the page navigates, and the pending text is gone. EditorShell autosave debounces for 1200ms; pagehide starts an async IndexedDB flush that does not complete reliably. Desktop tree navigation uses window.location.assign, and create Markdown, add assets, rename, download, and export also operate without first awaiting the pending editor commit.
acceptance_criteria: The UI never reports Saved while autosave has pending text. Reload/close either durably preserves pending text or explicitly prevents/warns about leaving. File switching, New Markdown, add assets, rename, download, export, and any route navigation await a durable flush before reading or changing workspace state. Chromium and WebKit regressions cover type-then-immediate-reload, type-then-immediate-file-switch, and fresh-content download/export.
notes: Implementation plan: make AutosaveController report Saving immediately, make flush drain pending and in-flight revisions with a success result, add a dirty beforeunload guard, and route every navigation/read/export/share action through one awaited flushPendingEditor boundary. Tests: autosave concurrency/failure units plus Chromium/WebKit immediate reload, file-switch/New Markdown, and export regressions.
close_reason: Implemented truthful autosave state and an awaited durability boundary for reload-sensitive navigation, mutations, downloads, exports, and sharing. Added concurrency/failure units and Chromium/WebKit regressions; all pass.

title: Enforce owner-accept invariant across live collaboration
description: Merged browser-owner collaboration currently accepts and autosaves remote ProseMirror steps. Comment-tier native/browser clients are also not gated from sendCollab. This bypasses the locked Sharing v3 invariant that only an explicit owner accept may mutate the owner file.
acceptance_criteria: Comment and view tiers cannot emit collab document steps. Suggest-tier remote edits are represented as durable suggestions requiring explicit owner accept; no remote collab transaction autosaves to the owner file. Owner-authenticated outbound collaboration remains available for read-only convergence. Native/browser hostile-client tests prove boundary enforcement.
notes: Approach: preserve owner-originated collaboration broadcasts for read-only convergence, but reject every remote ProseMirror document-step submit at the authenticated owner authority boundary (mailbox and direct). View/comment/suggest reviewer UIs remain selection-capable but cannot live-edit; suggest tier uses existing durable SuggestionCreated flow and explicit owner accept/apply. Add native/browser hostile-client tests, tier UI tests, and prove no remote collab transaction reaches saveEdits/workspace autosave.
close_reason: Enforced strict owner-accept authority across browser and native collaboration; reviewers remain read-only until explicit owner acceptance

title: Relay: preserve browser WebSocket Origin across Worker-to-DO forwarding
description: Real local Playwright against wrangler dev proved browser WebSocket upgrades arrive at RoomDO with Origin rewritten to the internal request origin (http://relay.attn.sh), not the browser page origin (http://localhost:8787). The DO therefore rejects allowBrowser=true rooms with ATTN_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN unless the relay's own origin is allowlisted, and production Worker-to-DO forwarding may similarly break https://attn.sh browser sockets or validate the wrong origin. Capture the edge Origin into a private Worker-overwritten header before stub.fetch, strip client spoofing, validate that preserved value in RoomDO, and add real/local Playwright plus spoof/disallowed/allowlisted regressions.
notes: Implemented fail-closed browser-origin trust boundary. Worker globally strips client X-Attn-Edge-Origin, then unconditionally writes v1.native / v1.browser.<base64url UTF-8 canonical origin> / v1.invalid for socket forwarding. RoomDO ignores rewritten standard Origin, validates only the private context, applies allowBrowser + exact allowlist policy, returns generic origin errors, and rejects missing/malformed internal context. Added strict codec tests and integration regressions for spoof overwrite, native sentinel, malformed/opaque origins, direct-DO missing context, and simulated standard-Origin rewrite. Independent security audit found no blockers; global private-header stripping hardening applied. Validation: typecheck exit 0; focused origin/CORS/WebSocket 70/70; full relay 382/382. Real local Wrangler + Playwright/Chromium passed with only http://localhost:8787 allowlisted (no relay.attn.sh workaround): health 200, two WS 101 upgrades, 65 replayed payloads, cursor close 4005/ATTN_CURSOR_TOO_OLD/resyncFromSeq 3. Used isolated local-only Wrangler config because Wrangler v3 rewrites Origin before Worker when production custom-domain routes are loaded.
close_reason: Fixed and verified by unit/integration/full relay tests plus real local Playwright WebSocket E2E

title: Review margin/panel does not mount on panelOpen toggle (reviewer can't see cards)
description: Found via real daemon E2E (attn --eval/--query). In a reviewer's shared-doc view, reviewStore.panelOpen flips to true (Cmd+J -> togglePanel(), and the auto-open at App.svelte:329 when a composer opens), but the right-rail aside stays data-state=closed and the {#if reviewStore.panelOpen} content (ReviewMargin overlay, data-slot=review-margin) never mounts — so the comment/suggestion margin CARDS (and thus the Reply/Resolve buttons) never render for the reviewer. The store value reads true; the <aside> in the {:else if hasSidebar} branch (App.svelte:2139-2177) doesn't react. Other reviewStore-driven UI (shared-doc banner, presence) DOES react, and App-local $state (the new selection toolbar) reacts — so it's specific to this aside's panelOpen binding. Repro: scripts/test-editorial-e2e.sh ('no margin card rendered'). Determine whether real users are affected (likely) and fix the reactivity/layout gating. Blocks the rendered Reply/Resolve UX even though the underlying review_resolve_comment/review_create_comment IPC verticals work (verified: events import on the owner).
notes: CONFIRMED REAL + reviewer-specific via real daemon (scripts/test-editorial-e2e.sh + isolated probe). Reviewer in shared-doc view: panelOpen=true (set via the reactive togglePanel() method) BUT the right-rail <aside data-state={reviewStore.panelOpen?'open':'closed'}> stays data-state=closed and the {#if reviewStore.panelOpen} content (ReviewMargin, data-slot=review-margin) never mounts -> comment/reply/resolve cards INVISIBLE to the reviewer. Owner is UNAFFECTED: isolated probe (owner on a folder) togglePanel() -> state=open + margin mounts. So the same <aside> binding to reviewStore.panelOpen reacts for the owner but not in the reviewer's shared-doc view (isReviewerViewingSnapshot). NOT an automation artifact (the auto-open at App.svelte:329 also set panelOpen=true when the composer opened, still no margin). Release BLOCKER: the new editorial UI (attn-bit/zhr/1rm) is invisible to reviewers without this. Next: find why the aside's panelOpen binding doesn't track in the reviewer layout (App.svelte ~2139 hasSidebar branch); likely a re-mount/keying or derived-chain issue tied to isReviewerViewingSnapshot.
close_reason: Fixed: ReviewMarginCard had a 'state' prop, so the $state rune added for the reply composer (attn-1rm) compiled as store auto-subscription (store_get($$props.state)) -> 'state.subscribe is not a function' thrown on every card render -> margin overlay never mounted (cards invisible). Renamed prop state->cardState + 2 call sites. Confirmed via extended automation (window error capture + unminified build): 0 $state()( in bundle, editorial E2E 11/0/0, reviewer margin card renders.

title: send_collab skip-relay optimization drops data when mesh is partial/flaky
description: THE no-TURN fix. send_collab (and the review-event send path) must route per-peer: send over a peer's direct DataChannel only when that specific pair is robustly Connected; for any peer WebRTC can't reach (symmetric NAT, no TURN), send a TARGETED relay copy (relay already routes by target.deviceId via deliverableTo/env_by_target — extend from signals to data envelopes). Receiver dedups by EventId/serverSeq so double-delivery over mesh+relay is harmless. Replaces the current all-or-nothing 'mesh complete -> skip relay' gate that silently drops un-meshed peers. Validated by the symmetric-NAT Docker harness (attn-orf).
notes: ROOT CAUSE OF 'collab doesn't converge in Docker' FOUND — it was NOT this skip-relay logic. It was a re-entrant agent deadlock (see attn-orf, commit f60cde1). With that fixed, collab converges 4/4 and routes channels=true relay=false (complete mesh, WebRTC-primary) — exactly the 'mesh complete -> skip relay' path. attn-7qv's per-peer relay fallback (decide_collab_routing: always-channels + relay-when-incomplete) is implemented + 4 unit tests pass, but STILL NOT integration-validated, because the Docker partition does not produce a partial mesh (the DataChannel forms anyway). To validate this P0 we must first make the partition FAITHFUL: block the peer-to-peer UDP path (default-DROP, allow only relay host-gateway:8787) so ICE genuinely fails and collab is forced onto relay-only. Until then, treat the per-peer fallback as plausibly-correct-but-unproven. The original user-reported 'sync feels broken' was most likely attn-cqk (reviewer margin not rendering), now fixed.
close_reason: VALIDATED end-to-end (commit). Faithful UDP-blackout partition: mesh never forms (all agents mailbox-only, live_direct_count=0) yet comment+collab converge 4/4 via relay alone. Baseline converges WebRTC-primary. Per-peer relay fallback proven for no-TURN symmetric-NAT.

title: /app/storage and workspace deep links 404; the service worker passes 404s through instead of serving the shell
description:
On the production build, `/app/storage` and every workspace deep link return **404**, and the service worker cannot compensate.

Measured: `curl /app/storage` -> 404, `/app/storage/` -> 404, `/app/w/<id>/<file>.md` -> 404. `dist-browser` emits only `app/index.html`, so these routes need host rewrite rules to serve the SPA shell.

**The service worker does not cover the gap, and this part is not a deploy question.**
`web/src/hosted/sw/sw.ts:96-116` is network-first and only falls back to the cached shell when `fetch` **throws**. A 404 is a *successful* HTTP response, so it is passed straight through to the page. Verified live: the SW was registered (controller present) and `/app/storage` still 404'd.

Consequences in the audited environment:
- The desk header's only action — the "Storage" button (DeskHome.svelte:118) — is a dead link.
- Reloading any workspace URL loses the workspace.

Whether attn.sh itself has the rewrite rules is a deploy-configuration question outside this build. The SW's inability to compensate is not — a navigation request that 404s should fall back to the cached app shell exactly as a network failure does. Fix the SW regardless of the host config, because the host config is the thing most likely to drift.

Add a route-level assertion to the e2e suite (`web/e2e/hosted-routes.spec.ts` already covers the landing) that fetches `/app/storage` and a workspace deep link and asserts a 200 with the app shell, so this cannot regress silently.

Audit caveat recorded for whoever picks this up: `StoragePage.svelte` could not be audited live because of this. Any storage-page contrast or layout numbers taken during this pass came from the server's 404 page and should be disregarded.

Suggested command: /impeccable harden

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
SERVICE-WORKER HALF FIXED. The deploy half is not mine to fix.

sw.ts navigation-network-first now falls back to the cached shell on a 404/410, not only when fetch
throws. A 404 is a successful HTTP response, so it was being passed straight through — which is why
the service worker could not compensate for a missing host rewrite, and why /app/storage and every
/app/w/<id>/<file> reload rendered the host's error page and lost the workspace.

Deliberately narrow: navigations only, status 404 or 410 only, and only when a shell is actually
cached. 500s, redirects and the offline path keep their existing behaviour, so this cannot mask a
real outage as a working page.

svelte-check 0 errors; sw bundle builds (81.93 kB); 97/97 unit test files pass.

STILL OPEN, and it needs someone with deploy access:
- dist-browser emits only app/index.html, so /app/storage and workspace deep links still 404 on a
  cold first visit, before any service worker is installed. The host rewrite rules are the real fix;
  the SW change above only covers returning visitors.
- Whether attn.sh and staging.attn.sh actually carry those rewrites is unverified from here. The
  worker (web/worker.ts) does rewriteToEntryDocument, so production may well be fine and this may be
  a dist-browser/static-serving artifact only — but I could not confirm that either way.
- No e2e assertion yet that /app/storage and a workspace deep link return 200 with the app shell.
  Worth adding to hosted-routes.spec.ts, which already covers the landing, so this cannot regress
  silently.

Also unblocked by this: StoragePage could not be audited live because of the 404 (noted in the
original finding). Any storage-page numbers taken during the audit came from the server's error page
and should be disregarded.

title: Desk at 200% zoom overflows to 612px and clips the header; mobile breakpoint deletes row metadata
description:
At 200% zoom the desk overflows to **612px on a 390px viewport** and clips the header row at both 390 and 1280. WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA) — the same class of failure filed against the home page, so the two are worth fixing in one session with one shared approach.

Three more responsive defects on the desk:

**The <=900px breakpoint deletes columns instead of reflowing them.** `.workspace-row .detail { display: none }` (app-shell.css:2363-2365) drops file count and last-edited, so on mobile three workspaces become byte-identical rows — name, "Local only", Rename, Delete. The list loses every distinguishing fact it had.

**One hard 3->1 column jump with no 2-column tier**, leaving 901-1100px ragged.

**The header runs edge-to-edge while the body is a 1300px centred column** — a 322px disagreement at 1920px. The chrome and the content do not share a measure.

Preserve what is right: **zero horizontal overflow at 320/375/390/414/768/1024/1280/1920** — `scrollWidth === clientWidth` at all eight, with no offending element at any width. That is genuinely good and rare, and the 200% failure above should be fixed without regressing it.

Suggested command: /impeccable adapt

---
EXACT ROOT CAUSE (desk audit):

  app-shell.css:9   .app-shell { grid-template-rows: 64px 1fr; }

A fixed 64px row cannot contain a header whose content grows to 76px at 200%. This single declaration
causes the failure at BOTH widths:

  390x844   scrollWidth 612 vs clientWidth 390 — horizontal scrolling required at the equivalent of
            320 CSS px. Overflowing elements: header.app-header 0/612, div.right 202/568, a.button
            400/568, main.desk 0/612, div.desk-title 32/580, h1 32/580, div.quick-actions 32/580 —
            i.e. everything. The "Storage" button is visually clipped at the top of the header.
            WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow (AA) and 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA).
  1280x900  no horizontal overflow, but the header still clips: scrollHeight 76 vs clientHeight 63.

FIX: grid-template-rows: minmax(64px, auto) 1fr, and let .app-header wrap — its children are already
flex-wrap-friendly (app-shell.css:12-26).

Also in the same family: media-query coverage gap. app-shell.css:118-125 (1.6fr 1fr 1fr) drops straight
to app-shell.css:2355-2357 (1fr) at <=900px. Between 901-1100px the 1fr tracks are ~250px and "Import
workspace" wraps to two lines while its siblings stay on one (measured at 1024), leaving a ragged card
row. No 2-column tier exists.

And: header and body sit on different measures. .desk is max-width 1300px centred (app-shell.css:90-95)
while .app-header is edge-to-edge padding 0 1.4rem (app-shell.css:17). At 1920 the Storage button lands
at x~1855 while the desk content's right edge is at 1533 — a 322px disagreement.
close_reason:
Fixed; horizontal overflow now clean at every breakpoint and both text sizes.

Four causes, all measured:
1. app-shell.css .app-shell had grid-template-rows: 64px 1fr — a fixed row cannot hold a header whose
   content grows with text size. Now minmax(64px, auto) 1fr.
2. The shell's single grid column was sized by its widest child, so the header's unwrapped content set
   a 612px floor that main.desk inherited. Added grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr).
3. .app-header and .app-header .right now flex-wrap; the header growing taller at 200% is correct,
   the page scrolling sideways is not.
4. .quick big and .empty-desk now break long strings (overflow-wrap). The mono meta line
   'UNTITLED.MD · NOT CREATED YET' carries 0.1em tracking and cannot shrink — it alone drove 87px
   past the card.
Also converted the desk's bare 1fr tracks (.quick-actions, .workspace-row, and their <=900px
overrides, plus .storage-grid) to minmax(0, 1fr), matching the idiom already used throughout the file.

MEASURED, documentElement scrollWidth - clientWidth:
                 100% text      200% text
  BEFORE  @390   clean          OVERFLOW 222px   header box 63 vs content 76 (clipped)
  AFTER   @320   clean          clean
          @390   clean          clean
          @768   clean          clean
          @1280  clean          clean            header box 89 vs content 89 (no clip)
          @1920  clean          clean

WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text and 1.4.10 Reflow now pass on the desk. Verified visually at 1280 light,
1280 dark and 390. svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit tests pass.

NOT in this change, still open in the epic: the <=900px breakpoint still hides .detail rather than
reflowing it, and there is still no 2-column tier between 901-1100px.

title: The desk shows no review state; WorkspaceSummary carries no review facts at all
description:
attn's whole claim is that humans and agents review the same document together. The desk — the surface the owner opens most — shows **no review state at all**.

The row exposes Local only / Shared / Backed up, but no open-comment count, no pending-suggestion count, no "an agent left 3 suggestions", no peer avatars, no unread indicator.

It is not just a rendering gap. `WorkspaceSummary` (web/src/hosted/app/types.ts:36-47) carries `markdownCount`, `assetCount`, `lastEditedLabel`, `sharing`, `sizeLabel`, `backupLabel`, `openPath` — and not one review fact. The data model has no place to put one.

A desk that lists **files** instead of **reviews in flight** is a file manager wearing attn's typeface. PRODUCT.md:44 makes "human and agent are peers in one thread" a design principle; the owner's home screen does not know that either exists.

This is the desk's equivalent of the home page's positioning gap (filed separately in this epic) — the same absence, one layer in.

Work involved:
- Extend `WorkspaceSummary` with review facts (open comments, pending suggestions, last activity, and who — human or agent).
- Surface them on the row in the resting state, where Rename/Delete currently sit.
- Decide the priority order: for a reviewer tool, "3 suggestions waiting" outranks "6 files" and probably outranks the last-edited timestamp.

Related question worth settling at the same time: what is "New workspace" doing on this screen at all? The landing already offers `/app#new` as a one-click path and `AppShell.createAndOpen()` (:67-98) makes it idempotent. Creation occupies 524px of prime real estate; opening occupies 200x28px of text. The ratio is backwards for a surface used daily.

Suggested command: /impeccable shape

title: The workspace row is four text islands: dead hover CSS, a text-sized open target, resident admin controls
description:
The workspace row is the payload — the thing the primary user is here for fifty times a week — and it is the least designed object on the page.

Measured at 1440: a 1185x68px row where "Project Gamma" ends at x=275, "1 file" sits at x=600, "Just now" at x=870. Roughly **250px of dead space between every column**, no column headers, nothing forming a scannable ledger. Grid is `1.2fr 0.65fr 0.65fr auto` (app-shell.css:163).

Four concrete defects:

1. **The hover state is dead CSS.** `a.workspace-row:hover` (app-shell.css:172) never matches — the element is a `<div>` (DeskHome.svelte:207; confirmed at runtime, `tagName === "DIV"`). The row has no hover state whatsoever; only the name underlines.

2. **The open target is text-sized.** `.row-open` wraps only the `<strong>` (DeskHome.svelte:222-224) — about 200x28px of an 80,000px² row.

3. **Row admin is resident chrome.** Rename and Delete are permanently rendered on every row (DeskHome.svelte:237-246); nothing is disclosed on hover or focus. At 3 workspaces that is 9 interactive controls in one undifferentiated block; at James's realistic 15 it is 45, and the three most-repeated words on screen become "Rename, Delete, Rename, Delete…".

4. **The weighting is inverted.** `.row-action` is 12.48px at weight 650 (app-shell.css:2508) while the adjacent data ("1 file", "Just now") is 13.12px at weight 400. The destructive administrative control is optically *heavier* than the content it acts on.

Fix: make the whole row the open target (a stretched-link pseudo-element over the row, with the actions raised above it in stacking order). Tighten the grid so metadata sits close-right of the name instead of drifting. Add a real row hover fill plus `:focus-within`. Reveal Rename/Delete on hover/focus-within only, so the resting row is name + recency + sharing state. Wrap the rows in `<ul>`/`<li>` (also tracked in the desk a11y issue).

Two adjacent defects in the same region:
- The delete confirm injects a ~190px full-width block **between** rows, shoving everything below it down and back up again on cancel — layout jitter in a list you scan. It also spans the full 1185px for a two-button question (DeskHome.svelte:249-271).
- `.row-action:hover` background is `color-mix(in srgb, var(--sheet) 70%, transparent)` (app-shell.css:2516) — near-invisible on PAPER.
- Dead code: `sharingLabel()` returns 'Shared · relay sees only ciphertext' (DeskHome.svelte:69-70) but that branch is unreachable — DeskHome.svelte:232 handles the 'shared' case before the fallback runs. A sign the row's state rendering was patched rather than modelled.

Suggested command: /impeccable shape
close_reason:
Fixed the four defects; the two that need a design decision are noted.

1. THE HOVER RULE WAS DEAD. 'a.workspace-row:hover' never matched because the element is a <div>, so
   the row had no hover state at all — only the name underlined. Now .workspace-row:hover,
   :focus-within, and [data-selected] all take a fill.
2. THE OPEN TARGET IS THE WHOLE ROW. .row-open::after stretches over it (about 200x28px before, in an
   80,000px² row — a Fitts's-law failure on the most repeated action in the product). .row-tail is
   raised above it so Rename and Delete stay independently clickable.
3. ROW ADMIN IS NO LONGER RESIDENT CHROME. The actions fade in on hover, focus-within, or selection.
   At a realistic workspace count the three most-repeated words on the desk were 'Rename, Delete,
   Rename, Delete…'. They remain in the tab order and available to assistive tech at all times — this
   is opacity, not display — and @media (hover: none) keeps them permanently visible on touch, where
   there is no hover to reveal them.
4. WEIGHTING — the actions are icons now (.2), so the 12.48px/650 text that outweighed the 13.12px/400
   data beside it is gone.

Verified visually: the resting row is name, file count, recency and sharing state; the actions appear
on the hovered row only.

Also closed with it: the list semantics and heading (.30), and the dead sharingLabel branch (.44).

NOT DONE, both design decisions rather than defects:
- The delete confirm still injects ~190px between rows, shifting everything below it. Making it a
  proper overlay or an inline slide changes the interaction model.
- The row's 250px column voids remain. Tightening the grid so metadata sits close-right of the name
  is a layout composition call, and it interacts with the mobile work in .33.

svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Desk on mobile: first workspace sits at y=813 in an 844px viewport; row actions are 48x28
description:
On a 390x844 viewport the desk puts its entire payload below the fold and shrinks its controls under the touch minimum.

**The first workspace name is off-screen on load.** Measured `.workspace-row` top = **813px in an 844px viewport**. Three 155px tiles stacked (app-shell.css:2355-2357) plus the 2.5rem/4rem margin pair on `.quick-actions` push the list past the fold — roughly 1.7 viewport heights of chrome before a document appears. (At 1440x900 the equivalent figure is 558px, 62% of the viewport, consumed before the first workspace name.)

**Row action targets are 57x28px and 48x28px**, measured on all six via `getBoundingClientRect`, with Delete sitting 24px from Rename. Well under 44x44, and the deletion is irreversible — mis-taps destroy workspaces.

**File count and last-edited are deleted on mobile.**
  app-shell.css:2363-2365   @media (max-width: 900px) { .workspace-row .detail { display: none } }
That removes the only recency signal from a list titled "Recently on this device". The mobile row shows name + "Local only" + Rename + Delete.

**The name gets 118px.** `.row-tail` claims ~240px of a 358px row (grid becomes `1fr auto` at app-shell.css:2359-2361), so "Project Beta Longer Name Here" wraps to three lines. The payload gets a third of the row; the admin controls get two thirds.

**The join panel's buttons break apart.** `.join-row { display:flex; gap:8px; flex-wrap:wrap }` (app-shell.css:2741-2745) with `min-width:240px` on the input (app-shell.css:2749) leaves "Join" beside the field and orphans "Cancel" onto its own line, left-aligned and visually detached.

**Header crowding is one string away from breaking.** Brand + badge + Storage on one line at 390px with `gap: 0.7rem` (app-shell.css:22-26). It fits with "Backup recommended"; the longer "Storage needs attention" state (AppHeader.svelte:25-26) will collide.

Fix direction: collapse the three action tiles to a single primary plus an overflow on mobile, keep the metadata (it is the reason the list exists), give the name the majority of the row, and move row admin behind a per-row overflow control sized to 44x44.

Suggested command: /impeccable adapt

title: 'Backup recommended' is painted in the safe-state green, and the desk offers no backup affordance
description:
The header badge shows a green dot and green text reading "Backup recommended". Green-on-green is the universal "you're fine" signal, attached to a message that means the user's work is one browser-storage eviction from gone. This is the "is my work safe?" moment for a local-first product with no cloud copy, and the desk currently gets it backwards.

Cause: `AppHeader.svelte:19-21` maps `best-effort` to `{ label: 'Backup recommended', warn: false }`, so it renders through `.local-badge { color: var(--green) }` (app-shell.css:47) — the identical treatment to the healthy `persistent` / "On this device" state. Only `warn: true` states get `--rust-deep` (app-shell.css:50-52).

Two DESIGN.md violations at once:
- **Quarantine Rule** — green belongs to the collaboration layer (suggestion/insertion) only, never to base chrome state.
- **INK theme** — `--green` resolves to `oklch(0.74 0.13 150)`, a saturated mint glowing on `oklch(0.148 0.014 255)` near-black, which the dark-theme guidance explicitly rejects.

It also fails the "never rely on colour alone" requirement in reverse: the colour actively contradicts the words.

Compounding the problem, there is **no export or backup affordance anywhere on the desk**. Every row says "Local only" in flat muted grey, and the remedy lives behind a "Storage" button that the copy never connects to.

Fix:
- `best-effort` is a caution, not a success. Set `warn: true` and introduce a third, neutral/caution badge treatment that is neither the collaboration green nor the destructive red — a muted neutral with a hollow dot reads as "attention" without borrowing a quarantined hue.
- Make the badge itself a link to `/app/storage` so the remedy is one click from the warning.
- Reserve `--green` strictly for suggestions.

Related state legibility gap: `Local only` / `Backed up` / `Shared` (DeskHome.svelte:67-76) are three unexplained states with no legend, and nothing on the desk explains what "Backup recommended" wants the user to *do*.

Suggested command: /impeccable colorize
close_reason:
Fixed. best-effort is now a caution tier of its own, and the badge links to the remedy.

AppHeader's badge returns a three-value tone instead of a boolean warn:
  persistent      -> ok       (green, filled dot)   'On this device'
  best-effort     -> caution  (muted ink, HOLLOW dot) 'Backup recommended'
  session-only / unavailable / quota-pressure -> warn (--danger-ink, filled dot)

Previously best-effort returned warn: false and so rendered in exactly the same green as the healthy
state — green-on-green is the universal 'you're fine' signal, attached to a message meaning the
user's work is one storage eviction from gone.

Two DESIGN.md violations closed with it: green is quarantined to the collaboration layer, so a
storage state was never entitled to it; and --green resolves to a saturated mint on INK's near-black
ground. Caution now uses muted ink, which is neither the collaboration hue nor the destructive one.

Not colour-only, per PRODUCT.md: the caution dot is HOLLOW (inset ring) while ok and warn are filled,
so the tiers differ in shape as well as hue.

THE REMEDY IS NOW ONE CLICK FROM THE WARNING — any non-ok badge renders as an <a href='/app/storage'>
rather than a <span>. The desk previously stated the problem and left the fix behind an unrelated
'Storage' button the copy never connected to. Verified live: tone='caution', tagName='A',
color=oklch(0.32 0.012 65).

The row-level 'Shared · relay sees only ciphertext' badge keeps green deliberately — that is the
collaboration layer, the one place the Quarantine Rule allows it.

STILL OPEN: there is still no export/backup affordance on the desk itself; the badge routes to the
Storage page rather than offering the action inline.

svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Desk a11y: Rename/Delete announce no workspace name; no list semantics; alertdialog without the contract
description:
Four accessibility defects on the desk, the first of which is data-loss-grade. **[P0] Rename and Delete have no accessible context.** Live DOM confirmed: DeskHome.svelte:237-246 No `aria-label`, no `aria-describedby`. Tabbing a 10-workspace desk announces "Rename button, Delete button, Rename button, Delete button…" with no indication of **which workspace is about to be destroyed**, and the deletion is explicitly irreversible. This is the single worst a11y defect on the page. Fix: `aria-label={`Delete ${workspace.name}`}` and the same for Rename. **[P1] No list semantics.** Verified zero `ul`, `ol` or `role="list"` inside `main.desk`. The list is an unstructured run of links and buttons — no "list, N items" announcement, no item position, no way to jump by list. Wrap the rows in `
    `/`
  • `. **[P1] `role="alertdialog"` without the modal contract.** DeskHome.svelte:250 declares the role, but focus is never moved into it, focus is not trapped, and Escape does not close it. A screen-reader user is told an alert dialog opened and then finds focus still on the Delete button behind it. Either implement the contract (move focus, trap it, Escape closes, restore focus) or drop the role and treat it as inline confirmation. **[P1] Escape does not close the join panel, and focus is never restored.** Verified live: the panel is still in the DOM after an Escape keypress — DeskHome.svelte:44-48 has no key handler, and `closeJoin()` does not return focus to the tile that opened it. Both violate DESIGN.md's Topmost-Escape Rule ("Escape closes exactly one layer… Every overlay stores focus on open and restores it on close"). Note the open half is already right: the panel correctly focuses its input on open (DeskHome.svelte:40-42). Only the close half is missing. Two smaller ones from the same pass: - `aria-label="A half-written Markdown sheet, waiting"` (DeskHome.svelte:275) is poetic prose describing a visual metaphor. A screen-reader user hears a region name that explains nothing about what to do and does not convey that this is the empty state. - The import error `

    ` (DeskHome.svelte:198-202) uses hardcoded inline `style` attributes, sits above the hidden file input, and has `role="alert"` but no association with the control that failed. - Only two landmarks on the page: HEADER and MAIN. No nav, no labelled section around the list. Preserve what is already right: focus-visible is complete and correct. A 16-stop Tab walk found every stop — brand, Storage, all three quick tiles, every `.row-open`, every `.row-action` — drawing a 2px solid ring in the theme accent, correctly recoloured to steel `oklch(0.72 0.1 220)` in INK. Nothing is `outline: none`. Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Fixed and verified by live browser probe on a populated desk. [P0] DESTRUCTIVE ACTIONS NOW NAME THEIR TARGET — Rename and Delete carry aria-label with the workspace name. Verified: 'Rename Untitled' / 'Delete Untitled'. Tabbing a multi-workspace desk previously announced 'Rename button, Delete button, Rename button…' with no indication of which workspace was about to be irreversibly deleted. LIST SEMANTICS — the rows are now
    /
  • , labelled by the section heading. Verified: 1 list, 1 item on a one-workspace desk. Previously a flat run of divs — no 'list, N items', no item position, no way to jump to it. THE POPULATED DESK HAS A HEADING AGAIN — 'Recently on this device' was a plain
    , so the empty desk exposed an

    and the populated desk exposed none: the more content the page had, the less structure it offered. Now an

    carrying the same class. Verified outline: H1 'Your desk' -> H2 'Recently on this device'. THE alertdialog NOW HAS THE CONTRACT IT ADVERTISES — aria-modal, tabindex=-1, focus moved in on open (use:autofocus), and focus restored to the invoking Delete button on cancel. Escape dismisses it. ESCAPE CLOSES THE TOPMOST LAYER — a keydown handler on the shell closes the delete confirm first, then the join panel, per DESIGN.md's Topmost-Escape Rule. closeJoin() now also restores focus to the tile that opened it; the open half was already correct (the panel focuses its input), only the close half was missing. Verified: join panel open->true, after Escape open->false, focus returned to the join-review trigger. Also folded in from .44 while in the same markup: the join tile now exposes aria-expanded and aria-controls, so its disclosure state is visible to assistive tech. svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass. NOT in this change: the import error

    is still positioned away from the control that failed, and there is still no aria-live announcement for rename/delete completion (tracked in .46).

title: Desk has no keyboard model at all (heuristic 7 scores 0/4) on a keyboard-first product
description:
The desk scores **0/4** on Nielsen heuristic 7 (Flexibility and Efficiency of Use). PRODUCT.md's primary user is James — "keyboard-first flow", "every action keyboard-reachable", "optimize for the hundredth review, not the first". This desk is optimised for the first.

Evidence: `DeskHome.svelte` contains exactly one keyboard handler — Enter/Escape inside the rename input (DeskHome.svelte:215-218). Grepping DeskHome / AppShell / AppHeader / StoragePage / OpenPage for `CommandPalette`, `keydown`, `metaKey`, `.key ===` returns nothing else.

Missing entirely: command palette, "/" filter, "n" for new, j/k navigation, type-ahead, search, sort, filter, multi-select, pinning, last-opened restore. There is no search, sort or filter control on the list at any viewport, and the sort order is never stated — "Recently on this device" implies recency but nothing confirms it.

Compounding it, the open target is the name text only: `.row-open` wraps only the `<strong>` (DeskHome.svelte:222-224), roughly 200x28px inside a 1185x68px row. A Fitts's-law failure on the single most repeated action in the product.

Ship three things, in this order:
1. A "/" or Cmd-K filter over workspace names that focuses on keypress and narrows `.workspace-row` live.
2. Up/Down to move a selection through rows, Enter to open. The rows already carry a stable `data-workspace-id` (DeskHome.svelte:207) to hang selection off.
3. Escape closing the topmost layer (join panel, then delete confirm) with focus restored to the invoking control, per DESIGN.md's Topmost-Escape Rule.

Then advertise the shortcut in the `.folio-label` row so it is discoverable.

Open question worth answering before building: what happens at 40 workspaces? No search, no sort, no pagination, no virtualisation, no grouping, 68px rows, 45+ resident controls. There is a number at which this desk stops working and nobody currently knows what it is.

Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Shipped the three things the finding asked for, verified end to end in the browser.

1. '/' FOCUSES A LIVE FILTER over workspace names, with the shortcut shown as a kbd hint in the field.
2. UP/DOWN MOVE A SELECTION through the filtered list, scrolling it into view; selection hangs off the
   data-workspace-id the rows already carried, and is marked with a 2px accent bar at the inset.
3. ENTER OPENS the selected workspace. ESCAPE clears the filter first, then falls through to the
   layer-closing behaviour added in .30.

VERIFIED in one session against three seeded workspaces (Alpha notes / Beta draft / Gamma plan):
  '/'            -> document.activeElement.id === 'workspace-filter'
  type 'Beta'    -> rows 3 -> 1
  ArrowDown      -> [data-selected] is 'Beta draft'
  Escape         -> filter cleared, rows back to 3

One real bug found by testing rather than by reading: the handler was first placed on the .app-shell
div, so a keypress with focus on <body> — which is the state the page loads in — never reached it.
'/' silently did nothing. Moved to <svelte:window>, which is the only correct scope for a page-wide
shortcut. Worth noting because the DOM-level version type-checked and looked right.

Guards: '/' is ignored while typing in any input/textarea/contenteditable, so it cannot hijack the
rename or invite fields; arrows are ignored while the delete confirm is open so they cannot move a
selection behind a modal; arrows still work FROM the filter field, so type-then-arrow needs no
mouse. Match counts are announced through a polite live region.

NOT DONE: no command palette, no bulk actions, no pinning, no last-opened restore, and the sort order
is still implicit. The finding listed those as further work; this is the floor it asked to ship first.

svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Landing image pipeline: hero sizes over-fetches the LCP by 1.5x and 7.5MB of dead PNG fallbacks ship
description: Two image-pipeline defects on the landing, both measured against the production build. **[P1] The hero `sizes` attribute overstates the LCP box by 1.5x.** web/src/hosted/landing/Hero.svelte:68 sizes="(max-width: 680px) calc(100vw - 2rem), (max-width: 1180px) 72vw, 920px" The `.window img` box measures **614px** at every viewport >= 1180px (the hero grid is `minmax(500px,0.95fr) minmax(540px,1.05fr)` inside a 1296px content box, less `.window { inset: 24px 0 20px 30px }`). The attribute claims 920px, so the browser over-selects: 1440 @1x box 614px, needs 614 device px -> served 1280w (40,852 B); 768w (21,513 B) suffices WASTE 19,339 B 1440 @2x box 614px, needs 1228 device px -> served 1920w (45,170 B); 1280w suffices WASTE 4,318 B 1920 @2x box 647px, needs 1295 device px -> served 1920w correct 390 @3x box 346px, needs 1038 device px -> served 1280w correct The 1180 branch errs the other way: at a 1000px viewport the stage measures ~870px but `72vw` claims 720px — 21% under-served, so the image renders soft on retina laptops between 681 and 1180 CSS px. Recommended: `sizes="(max-width: 680px) calc(100vw - 2rem), (max-width: 1180px) calc(100vw - 5rem), 620px"` **[P1] 7.5 MB of unusable raw PNG fallbacks ship to production.** imports at Hero.svelte:9-10, HowItWorks.svelte:4-5, NativeSection.svelte:5-6; consumed at ResponsiveScreenshot.svelte:24 (`src={fallback}`) `dist-browser/assets` carries six raw 1920x1440 PNGs totalling 7,773,333 B: collab-dark 979,583 · collab-light 1,050,683 · editor-dark 1,580,143 editor-light 2,046,763 · share-dark 934,152 · share-light 1,182,009 Zero PNG requests were observed across four device profiles — AVIF-capable browsers never touch them. But a non-AVIF client (Safari <16.4, Firefox <93) pulls a 2.0 MB PNG into a 631px box, roughly 50x oversized, and there is no smaller step to degrade to because the `` carries no `srcset` of its own (only `` does). Recommended: generate a 1280w WebP or quality-80 JPEG as the `fallback` prop (~60-90 KB each) and drop the PNGs from the bundle. Bounds the worst case at ~90 KB and removes 7.5 MB from every Pages asset upload. Context — the rest of the image pipeline is genuinely good and should be preserved: AVIF with a proper srcset ladder, correct `loading`/`fetchpriority`/`decoding` per position, and lazy-loading verified working (editor AVIF deferred and fetched at 2357 ms on scroll). Suggested command: /impeccable optimize

title: 200% text scaling breaks the home page: 184px horizontal scroll and an unreachable CTA at 390px
description:
At 200% text on a 390px viewport the home page produces **184px of horizontal scroll** (scrollWidth 574 vs clientWidth 390), the nav's "New workspace" CTA is sliced by the right viewport edge and becomes unreachable, and the h1 clips "documents." mid-word. Loss of content AND functionality — WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text (AA).

Method: `page.addStyleTag({content:'html{font-size:200%}'})` at 390 and 1280. At 1280 there is no horizontal scroll; the defect is mobile-only for the grids, but the nav defect appears at both.

**Cause 1 — four grid tracks declared `1fr` instead of `minmax(0, 1fr)`.** `1fr` is `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, so the track floors at its content's min-content width and physically cannot shrink below it.

  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:236  .entry-strip
  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:290  .chapter-head
  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:318  .steps
  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:390  .surfaces
  (plus the <=680px overrides at :643-646, :664-667, :684-686)

Measured overflow per element at 390/200%:
  article.surface x2 .......... 163px past the viewport
  .surface h3 / p / ul / li ... 115px
  span.surface-label .......... 27px
  chapter-head children, h2, p.chapter-intro ... 26px
  div.nav-right, a.button.primary ... 24px
  a.entry x3 .................. 22px

Worst offender is `.surfaces`, whose `<li>` items are mono (landing.css:442-447): "→ Installable for offline launch" at 200% mono sets a min-content floor 163px wider than the viewport.

**The fix is already present in this file.** `.local-note` at landing.css:108-110 uses `repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr))` correctly. Applying `minmax(0, 1fr)` to the four grids above resolves every row in that table except `.nav-right`.

**Cause 2 — the nav uses a fixed `height`, so its own contents overflow it.**
  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:14   .site-nav { height: 70px }
  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:577  .site-nav { height: 64px }  (<=680px)

Measured at 200% text: box 70px vs scrollHeight 79px at 1280; box 64px vs scrollHeight 92px at 390. The CTA (min-height 46px from chrome.css:107, plus scaled padding) protrudes past the nav's `border-bottom`, which cuts through the button — and because the nav is `position: sticky` with `backdrop-filter`, the overflowing button then paints over hero content as the page scrolls. Use `min-height` and let `.nav-right` (landing.css:40-44) wrap or shrink.

Note what does NOT fail: WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow passes — tested at a 320px viewport (the 1280@400% equivalent), scrollWidth === clientWidth === 320. And at default text size there is **zero** horizontal overflow at 320/375/390/414/768/1024/1280/1920, verified by both document metrics and a full per-element bounding-box sweep. This defect is specific to text scaling.

Suggested command: /impeccable adapt
close_reason:
Fixed; horizontal overflow now clean at all eight widths at both text sizes.

Five causes, found by iterating the measurement rather than assuming the audit's list was complete:
1. Four grids declared bare 1fr (= minmax(auto,1fr), floors at min-content): .entry-strip,
   .chapter-head, .steps, .surfaces — plus .native-grid and the single-column mobile overrides.
   All now minmax(0, …), matching .local-note which already did it correctly.
2. .site-nav used a fixed height (70px / 64px), so it clipped its own contents at 200%
   (box 70 vs content 79). Now min-height.
3. .site-nav and .nav-right could not wrap, so the brand + links + CTA row set a floor wider than
   the viewport. This was the largest single contributor and was NOT in the original finding —
   it only surfaced after the grids were fixed.
4. The display headings could not break a long word ('documents.'), overflowing by 46px at 390.
   Added overflow-wrap: break-word to the h1/h2/h3/p rule.
5. The install command is one unbreakable token. .code now has min-width: 0 and .code > span
   scrolls internally, per DESIGN.md's Wide-Sheet Rule ('oversized tables/code scroll inside it').
   .footer-links wraps.

MEASURED, documentElement scrollWidth - clientWidth at 200% text:
        BEFORE            AFTER
  320   (untested) 221px  clean
  375   —                 clean
  390   184px             clean
  414   —                 clean
  768   143px             clean
  1024  —                 clean
  1280  clean             clean   (nav box 89 vs content 89 — no longer clipped)
  1920  —                 clean
100% text remains clean at every width. WCAG 1.4.4 and 1.4.10 now pass on the landing.

Verified visually at 1280 light, 1280 dark and 390 — no regression; the mobile masthead still uses
its two-tier h1. The four-line ragged mobile masthead is pre-existing and tracked separately in .17.

97/97 unit test files pass; svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Dark-mode visitors see ~1.2s of paper-white before INK applies (no prefers-color-scheme fallback)
description:
A dark-mode visitor gets a full paper-white page before INK arrives. Measured frame-by-frame on the production build at 300 kbps with a dark-preference UA:

  t =   14 ms   rgb(18,18,18)     UA dark canvas, no CSS yet
  t = 2645 ms   rgb(226,223,215)  CSS painted — PAPER, the wrong theme
  t = 3842 ms   rgb(9,13,19)      JS finally stamped .dark

That is roughly 1.2 seconds of full-page wrong-theme paint. On a faster connection it is shorter but still present; it is not a race that sometimes goes the right way, it is structural.

Mechanism, confirmed:
- The built page has four blocking `<link rel="stylesheet">` in `<head>`, so CSS paints the PAPER ground before any script runs.
- No stylesheet carries a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` fallback. Verified: `grep -n "prefers-color-scheme" web/src/tokens.css web/src/hosted/chrome.css web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css` returns nothing. The INK theme is driven entirely by the `.dark` class / `data-theme` attribute.
- That class is only stamped when the deferred `type="module"` bundle runs `initTheme()` (web/hosted/landing.ts:13, web/src/hosted/theme.svelte.ts).

The native app solves exactly this with an inline pre-paint script (web/index.html:7-31), whose own comment names the goal: keeping "a dark-mode user from seeing a frame of paper white on every launch". The hosted CSP forbids inline scripts (theme.svelte.ts:3-6 says so explicitly), and nothing replaced the mechanism when the constraint changed.

Note the inconsistency this creates: `web/hosted/index.html` already ships `<meta name="theme-color">` with a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` variant, so the browser chrome flips correctly while the page underneath does not.

Fix options, roughly in order of preference:
1. Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block that applies the INK token values when no explicit `data-theme` is set. Pure CSS, no script, correct at first paint, and the JS toggle continues to override it. This is the smallest correct fix.
2. Serve a CSP nonce for a tiny pre-paint inline script, matching the native app's approach.
3. Have the edge worker stamp `data-theme` from the `Sec-CH-Prefers-Color-Scheme` client hint.

Option 1 needs care: the tokens must respond to "no explicit preference + OS dark" without breaking the explicit light override. Test all four combinations — OS light/dark crossed with stored preference light/dark/absent.

Applies to every hosted entry, not just the landing: /app and /review load the same token stack.

Suggested command: /impeccable polish
close_reason:
Fixed and verified by frame capture.

MECHANISM: added a pre-paint inline theme stamp to every hosted entry, admitted by CSP source hash.
- src/lib/hosted/theme-preflight.ts — the script (one copy) + its sha256, with the rationale.
- vite.browser.config.ts injectThemePreflight() — stamps it head-prepend at build AND serve, so dev
  matches production. One source, three entries, no drift.
- src/lib/hosted/csp.ts — script-src now carries 'sha256-dlo6xal0...'. A hash admits exactly those
  bytes; strictly narrower than a nonce and unusable by injected markup.
- scripts/theme-preflight-hash.mjs — regenerates the hash.
- csp.test.ts — recomputes the hash from the script and fails on drift, plus asserts script-src never
  gains 'unsafe-inline' or a nonce. Without this guard a drifted hash silently blocks the script and
  the flash returns with no error anywhere.

MEASURED, same method as the finding (300 kbps, dark-preference UA, CDP screencast):
  BEFORE  t=  14ms UA canvas · t=2645ms rgb(226,223,215) PAPER — wrong theme · t=3842ms rgb(9,13,19) INK
          => ~1.2 s of full-page paper-white
  AFTER   t=  16ms UA canvas · t=3321ms rgb(9,13,19) INK
          => zero wrong-theme frames; first painted frame is already INK (verified visually, not just
             by pixel probe)

WHY NOT THE CSS FALLBACK: a @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) block would duplicate ~90 lines of INK
tokens — guaranteed to drift — and cannot see localStorage, so a visitor on a light OS who explicitly
chose dark would still flash. The inline stamp covers both.

Applies to all three hosted entries (/, /app, /review), which was the point: they share the token stack.

97/97 unit tests pass; svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Mobile navigation disappears entirely below 680px with no replacement
description:
At <=680px the entire navigation disappears with no replacement:

  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:580-582
    .nav-link { display: none; }

There is no hamburger, no sheet, no bottom bar. At 390px the nav is: brand, theme toggle, primary CTA. "How it works", "Native app", "Your desk" and "GitHub" become unreachable, and the visitor gets roughly 6,100px of scroll with zero navigation.

The two controls that remain are both undersized and both pinned top-right — the hardest zone to reach one-handed on a 6.1" phone:
  theme toggle   32.8 x 32.8  (chrome.css:144-154)
  primary CTA    126.6 x 40.6 (landing.css:588-591) — 3.4px under the 44px minimum

Compounding, at 390px the masthead breaks into four ragged lines because Hero.svelte:34 hard-codes the split with `<span>` elements, leaving "desk" orphaned on a short line while lines 3-4 drop to 0.72em mid-thought (landing.css:602-604). And `text-wrap: balance` applied globally to every `p` (landing.css:67-72) leaves the six-line lede with a ragged short tail exactly where attention is thinnest.

Fix:
- Ship a mobile nav. A bottom-anchored action bar is the better answer than a hamburger here, because it also moves the primary CTA into thumb reach.
- Raise the remaining touch targets to 44px (tracked in the sibling touch-target issue in this epic; that fix and this one must land together).
- Replace the hard `<span>` break with `text-wrap: balance` and let the two type tiers break on a container query rather than a hard-coded split.

Suggested command: /impeccable adapt

title: Home page asserts E2E encryption four times but never demonstrates it; no threat model or security link
description:
End-to-end encryption is the product's entire reason to exist, and the page asserts it four times in prose without ever showing it once.

Assertions: Hero.svelte:37-38, Hero.svelte:78, HowItWorks.svelte:52-53, HowItWorks.svelte:77-80.

What is missing: there is no threat model, no "what the relay actually sees" visual, no link to the crypto, no security page. Nav.svelte:15 and Footer.svelte:9 both point at a bare repo root. A skeptical reader — which is the entire target market for a local-first tool — finds nothing to evaluate, so the claim reads as marketing.

Compounding it, the asset carrying the emotional climax ("A room exists only after you press Share.", HowItWorks.svelte:65-73) is a screenshot of a modal over a dimmed grey document — a desaturated slab dropped into a warm paper page. It also has a stray blue OS focus ring baked into it on "Advanced options": a non-attn accent colour shipped in a marketing asset.

PRODUCT.md:42 asks for the guarantee to be "quietly evident in the UI... without turning into a security-theater badge wall". The page has achieved the second half and skipped the first.

Fix direction:
- Replace the dimmed-modal capture with a purpose-built two-panel visual: the document on the left, the ciphertext the relay actually stores on the right, with the `#key=` fragment marked "never sent". One demonstrated fact beats four assertions.
- Add a /security or /how-it-works link in nav and footer pointing at a real threat model.
- Then delete two of the four prose assertions — the visual does that work.

Suggested command: /impeccable shape

title: Hero screenshot is cropped through its own text on both edges (object-fit: cover)
description:
The hero screenshot is the page's only evidence and its intended peak, and it is visibly cropped through its own content on both edges. Verified by reading the rendered capture, not just the CSS.

At 1440px the left edge clips the file tree mid-word — the visible strings are "-cap-...", "er files", "lan.md". The right edge slices the review cards mid-sentence ("Can we open this to the whole waitlist, not" — the rest is gone), truncates their state badges to "CO" and "S", and cuts off the window frame so the rounded chrome never closes on the right.

Root cause, single and shared with the CLS defect below:

  web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css:172-178
    .window img { width:100%; height:100%; object-fit: cover; object-position: center top; }

`cover` fills a box narrower than the source aspect by discarding the sides. The box is narrower because `web/src/hosted/landing/ResponsiveScreenshot.svelte:26-27` hard-codes `width="1920" height="1440"` (ratio 1.333) for every caller, while the hero actually renders at 542x529 (ratio 1.025) — measured on the production build.

So there are two symptoms from one cause:
1. **The crop** (the serious one): a precision tool whose flagship screenshot is mis-cropped refutes its own claim in the same frame.
2. **The CLS reservation**: the browser reserves a 4:3 box and paints a 1:1 one, on the only `loading="eager"` image on the page. The other two screenshots are fine — share renders 678x508 (1.335) and editor 631x473 (1.334), both matching their declared ratio.

Fix: either switch `.window img` to `object-fit: contain` with the frame sized to the asset's true aspect, or crop the source deliberately at authoring time so the composition is intentional at every breakpoint. Either way, pass real intrinsic dimensions through ResponsiveScreenshot as props instead of hard-coding 1920x1440.

Check whether the documented landing perf gate (referenced in the Hero.svelte:56-58 comment as asserting both the CLS box and the AVIF payload) is actually catching the mismatch — if it is not, that gate has a hole.

Also in this asset: the hero shows only human "Reviewer" suggestion cards and no agent, which is the visual half of the positioning gap filed separately in this epic. Reshooting for the crop is the moment to fix that too.

Positive findings worth preserving: all 3 images carry alt text and width/height, the hero is correctly eager with fetchpriority=high, the other two are lazy, and AVIF-with-PNG-fallback plus a proper sizes attribute is already in place.

Suggested command: /impeccable polish

title: Home page chrome misses 44x44 touch targets in 8 controls; only .button carries a size floor
description:
Eight interactive controls fall under the 44x44 CSS px target at mobile widths (320 and 390 — measured identical at both). WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is 24x24 AA; 2.5.5 Enhanced is 44x44. Several of these also fail the 24px AA floor on one axis.

Measured on the production build, clean page (no detector injection):

  36.8 x 18   footer a "GitHub"          <- 41% of target height
  32.0 x 18   footer a "Issues"          <- 41%
  66.5 x 18   footer a "Contributing"    <- 41%
  40.0 x 23.4 button.code-copy "Copy" (brew)   <- 53%
  40.0 x 23.4 button.code-copy "Copy" (npx)    <- 53%
  32.8 x 32.8 button.icon-button "Toggle theme"  <- 75%, both axes
  80.4 x 29   a.brand "attn"
  126.6 x 40.6 a.button.primary "New workspace"  <- 3.4px short on height only

At 768 and 1280 the four `.nav-link` items also miss (20px tall).

The diagnosis is clean and the fix is systemic: `.button` at web/src/hosted/chrome.css:107 already sets `min-height: 46px`, and every control that uses `.button` passes. Every miss above is a control that does NOT use the class — nav links, the brand, the icon button, code-copy, footer links.

So this is not eight separate bugs. It is one missing rule: hit-target sizing lives on `.button` only, and the rest of the page's chrome was never brought under it.
